challengeFindings.title: An audit run that follows its prompt overwrites its own finished report: `steps stub --result-file --to=<Create>` replaces the anchored audit report (Probe Steps, Findings, Report, Project Instructions) with the short summary

A ledger append that crashes between its intent and its receipt can never be reconciled once its invocation goes stale, so the committed pending intent blocks `ledgers union`, compact, migrate and every `--correction-of` on that ledger for good

Feeding the audit `ledgerRows` the engine prints straight into `ledgers append --invocation` is refused, because each row's `by.step` is `audit-<slug>` while the standalone invocation vouches for `audit:<slug>`; the integration test hides this by stripping `by`

A resumed re-trigger push on a feature branch force-overwrites a commit someone else pushed, whenever any fetch already moved `origin/<branch>` to it: the remote-movement guard only blocks when the tracking ref is stale, which is exactly when `--force-with-lease` would have failed anyway

After a crash leaves part of a prepared block in the ledger and the lock is cleared as the error message advises, a friction or plain append lands next (neither checks pending intents), and reconciling the operation then takes the 'none of ours landed: prepare afresh' branch and appends rows that already landed a second time

An agent that retries a lost `--issue-operation` append with the same rows but a different JSON key order gets a new engine-issued operation id and appends every row a second time, because the request hash is `JSON.stringify` of the raw rows, not a canonical form

Audit ledger keys the engine derives are `<slug>-<title>`, while `bkit-audit-generate.md` defines new keys as `audit-<slug>-<content-slug>` and closes stale rows by the `audit-<slug>-` prefix, so rows the engine keys are never closed by later audit runs
A result file that is just `{}` (or omits `evidenceComplete` and `body`) renders a `Verdict: PASS` challenge or review artifact with an empty body, because `evidenceComplete` defaults to true

On a fresh consumer with no `docs/failures.jsonl` (coverage `missing`) or a ledger holding one malformed line (coverage `partial`), the prompts' 'follow `nextCursor` until `coverage.clean` is true' never terminates and names no route, so the agent loops, stops, or quietly treats the scan as clean
A hand-edited `--cursor` with a negative offset passes `decodeCursor` (any integer) and `rows.slice(-n, ...)` returns rows from the end of the scan as if they were the next page

Every operation-bound append writes its full row block twice into the committed `.bkit/ledger-operations.jsonl` (intent and receipt `detail`), which no compaction trims and which every later append parses whole twice

Every issued invocation commits the developer's absolute checkout paths (home directory and username, e.g. `/Users/<name>/...`) into the tracked run `status.jsonl`, which ships in consumer repo history and bkit's public repo.

Ledger-operation intents and receipts live in the committed, union-carried `.bkit/ledger-operations.jsonl`, not the private git-common outbox the plan names. A crash, or a branch that commits a receipt-less intent row, then propagates on merge and blocks `ledgers union` (worktree teardown), `ledgers compact` and the upgrade-path `migrateLedgers` in every checkout. The replay that would clear it needs the original request, which no other checkout can reproduce.

A line break in a header-bound result value (`report`, `issue` or `parent` in an audit result, or any free-text judgment) injects forged header lines and an early `<!-- verdict:end -->`. For example, a multi-line `report` that adds `Findings: CRITICAL 0 · HIGH 0 · MEDIUM 0 · LOW 0` makes `readHeader` read zero findings over the engine-derived `CRITICAL 1`. Because the cut-off header carries no `Fingerprint`, `fingerprintProblem` treats the artifact as hand-written and skips the stale check.

A replayed operation returns its stored receipt (`replayed: true`, exit 0) without checking that the target ledger still holds the receipted rows. After a branch switch, rebase, revert, or a receipt carried in from another checkout, a finding the caller believes is recorded is silently missing.

A standalone invocation's `<id>.corrections.jsonl` is created in the outbox with default permissions (typically world-readable 0644), unlike the 0600 receipt beside it. This breaks the `docs/security.md` contract that invocation files under Git-common `bkit-outbox` are private.
